bookTitle: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis

facts.statement: A draining demand anomaly is a multi-bar uptrend pattern where prices continue to rise with expanding spreads, but accompanying volume progressively falls, revealing that buying pressure is draining away and the market is overbought.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: A multi-bar anomaly in an uptrend where prices continue to rise with expanding spreads, but accompanying volume progressively falls... reveals that buying pressure is draining away.

facts.statement: Under Wyckoff's law of effort versus result, rising price spreads combined with falling volume constitute a structural anomaly and market weakness, confirming that major operators are no longer supporting the move.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Rising Price Spreads + Falling Volume = Anomaly / Market Weakness.

facts.statement: In Coulling's Figure 4.16 sequence, Candle 1 shows a narrow spread up candle validated by low volume, while Candle 2 forms a modestly wider spread up candle accompanied by high volume, signaling that high effort failed to produce a wide spread because insiders are selling.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Candle 1: A narrow spread up candle accompanied by low volume... Candle 2: A modestly wider spread up candle accompanied by high volume... Insiders are selling out into retail demand.

facts.statement: Candle 3 displays a wide spread up candle with lower volume than Candle 2 (two anomalies: spread/volume divergence and falling trend volume), while Candle 4 shows an even wider spread on lower volume, marking a total breakdown of effort versus result.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Candle 3: A wide spread up candle, but with lower volume than Candle 2... Candle 4: An extremely wide spread up candle accompanied by even lower volume... Total breakdown of Effort vs. Result.

facts.statement: The first clear sign of insider distribution during an uptrend is a modest spread up candle accompanied by high volume, indicating that buying enthusiasm is meeting heavy hidden resistance.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: High volume on a modest spread up candle during a trend is the first signal of insider distribution.

facts.statement: An exhausting volume anomaly occurs during a rapid market sell-off (price waterfall) when price spreads continue to widen downward while volume steadily decreases, signaling that selling pressure is exhausting and the market is oversold.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Occurs during a price waterfall when price spreads continue to widen downward while volume steadily decreases. This signals that selling pressure is exhausting and the market is becoming oversold.

facts.statement: Unlike physical gravity where objects fall under their own weight, financial markets require increasing volume and effort to fall just as they do to rise, meaning falling markets on diminishing volume lack sustainable bearish pressure.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Unlike physical gravity, financial markets require increasing volume (effort) to fall, just as they do to rise.

facts.statement: In Figure 4.17, Candle 2 shows a marginally wider down candle with very high volume (massive effort generating minimal drop due to buyer absorption), while Candles 3 and 4 show wide down spreads on lower and lower volume, proving bearish exhaustion.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Candle 2: A marginally wider spread down candle with high to very high volume... Candles 3 and 4: Wide spread down candles accompanied by lower/average volume... proving bearish exhaustion.

facts.statement: Wyckoff's three-step framework structures market analysis across three sequential tiers: Micro (evaluating individual candles), Macro (contextualizing against adjacent bars), and Global (evaluating the complete chart structure and support/resistance).

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: A structured, multi-tier process for evaluating market context by expanding perspective from an individual candle to the entire chart.

facts.statement: VPA operates like a camera zoom lens in reverse—starting close-up on a single bar (Micro), zooming out to local candle groups (Macro), and finally zooming out fully to the global chart context and broader market structure.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: VPA begins zoomed in on a single subject (Micro) and gradually zooms out to capture the complete picture (Macro to Global).

facts.statement: A micro or macro anomaly appearing across only a few candles typically results in nothing more than a minor pullback unless backed by a larger global cause in accordance with Wyckoff's Second Law of Cause and Effect.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: A micro/macro anomaly on a few candles usually results only in a minor pullback unless backed by a larger global cause (Wyckoff's Second Law: Cause and Effect).

facts.statement: Traders must never trade a single-candle anomaly in isolation; initial warning signals must be validated and confirmed by subsequent candles and contextualized against broader technical structural levels.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Never trade a single candle anomaly in isolation; validate it against adjacent bars (Macro) and key technical structural levels (Global).

generalAssumptions: Market price manipulation is structurally transparent on the volume tape.
Effort versus result governs institutional capital movement.
